narrativeProgression.description: Interviewer 1 outlines the context for the discussion, listing events that happened in 2020 related to Putin and his power.

Interviewee provides a detailed analysis of the events, arguing that while they have weakened Putin's position in the long run, his power remains strong in the short term due to the pandemic and the lack of organized opposition.
The conversation shifts to the upcoming parliamentary elections, with the interviewee expressing concerns about potential fraud and manipulation by the current government.

Interviewee further elaborates on the strategies expected from the Russian government to secure victory in the elections, including manipulating voter registration, introducing online voting, and diversifying the image of the ruling party.

Full interview at: https://youtu.be/bKdOUkum3BY
In this segment we discuss whether Putin can maintain his grip on power in the long term, as well as the impact of the Belarus protests on Russia. This is an excerpt from the interview with Dr. Sergei Guriev, leading Russian economist, political dissident and chief economist of the European Bank of Development and Reconstruction (EBRD). The interview centred around the political and economic future of Russia.
